title: Lines
parentNote: Write a few capital letters (L, T, V, X, E, H) together and ask him to trace each straight part with a finger while counting — that's exactly what this unit tests.
learnBullets: **Open** figures (ends don't meet) vs. **closed** figures (ends meet)
**Line of symmetry** — a line that divides a shape into two matching halves
learnItFirst:
```
———      Straight line
〰️      Curved line

—        Horizontal line   (flat, left to right)
|        Vertical line     (straight up and down)
/        Slanting line     (diagonal)
```

**Open vs. Closed figures:**
```
▲  (closed — starts and ends at the same point)
⌣  (open — starts and ends at different points)
```

**Line of symmetry:** an imaginary line where, if you fold the shape along it, both halves match exactly.
```
   |
 ▲   →  fold down the middle, both sides match!
```

### 🧠 How to Solve — 3 Easy Steps
1. **Look** — is the line straight or does it curve?
2. **Check the direction** — flat (horizontal), up-down (vertical), or diagonal (slanting)?
3. For symmetry — **imagine folding** the shape in half. Do both sides match exactly?

questions.content: Which of these is a STRAIGHT line: "———" or "〰️"?
questions.why: A straight line has no bends or curves

questions.content: Which of these is a CURVED line: "———" or "〰️"?
questions.why: A curved line bends smoothly

questions.content: A horizontal line goes:
questions.why: A horizontal line is flat, like the horizon

questions.content: A vertical line goes:
questions.why: A vertical line stands straight up

questions.content: A slanting (oblique) line goes:
questions.why: A slanting line is tilted, neither flat nor straight up

questions.content: Which of these is a horizontal line: "—" or "|"?
questions.why: This line is flat, so it is horizontal

questions.content: Which of these is a vertical line: "—" or "|"?
questions.why: " | This line stands straight up, so it is vertical

questions.content: Which of these is a slanting line: "/" or "—"?
questions.why: This line is tilted, so it is slanting

questions.content: A CLOSED figure starts and ends at:
questions.why: A closed figure's starting and ending points meet

questions.content: An OPEN figure/curve starts and ends at:
questions.why: An open curve's ends do not meet

questions.content: Which is a CLOSED figure: a triangle ▲ or an open arc "⌣"?
questions.why: A triangle's sides meet, forming a closed figure

questions.content: Which is an OPEN figure: a circle ● or a "C" shape?
questions.why: A "C" shape has a gap — its ends do not meet

questions.content: The capital letter "L" is made up of how many straight lines?
questions.why: "L" has one vertical line and one horizontal line

questions.content: The capital letter "T" is made up of how many straight lines?
questions.why: "T" has one horizontal line and one vertical line

questions.content: The capital letter "V" is made up of how many slanting lines?
questions.why: "V" has two slanting lines meeting at the bottom

questions.content: The capital letter "X" is made up of how many slanting lines?
questions.why: "X" has two slanting lines crossing each other

questions.content: A square is made up of how many straight lines (sides)?
questions.why: A square has 4 straight sides

questions.content: A triangle is made up of how many straight lines (sides)?
questions.why: A triangle has 3 straight sides

questions.content: Which of these letters has NO straight lines at all (fully curved)?
questions.why: "O" is a full curve, with no straight parts

questions.content: A line of symmetry divides a shape into:
questions.why: Folding along the line of symmetry gives two matching halves

questions.content: Does the capital letter "A" have a line of symmetry (a middle line where both sides match)?
questions.why: "A" looks the same on both sides of its middle vertical line

questions.content: Does the capital letter "F" have a line of symmetry?
questions.why: "F" does not look the same on both sides of any line

questions.content: Does a circle have a line of symmetry?
questions.why: A circle can be folded along any line through its centre and still match

questions.content: Does a square have a line of symmetry?
questions.why: A square has several lines of symmetry

questions.content: Which of these letters is made ONLY of straight lines: "S" or "Z"?
questions.why: "Z" is made only of straight lines; "S" has curves

questions.content: How many straight lines make up the capital letter "E" (top, middle, bottom, and the side)?
questions.why: "E" has 1 vertical line + 3 horizontal lines (top, middle, bottom)

questions.content: How many straight lines make up the capital letter "H" (two sides and the middle bar)?
questions.why: "H" has 2 vertical lines + 1 horizontal middle bar

questions.content: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle (non-square) have?
questions.why: A rectangle has 1 horizontal and 1 vertical line of symmetry

questions.content: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.why: A square has 1 horizontal + 1 vertical + 2 diagonal lines of symmetry

questions.content: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle (all sides equal) have?
questions.why: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry, one from each corner
